narration.text: Abram came back from Egypt rich in sheep, goats, silver and gold. And his nephew Lot was rich too.
And there was a strife between the herdmen of Abram’s cattle and the herdmen of Lot’s cattle: and the Canaanite and the Perizzite dwelled then in the land.
Two families, one pasture. The shepherds were fighting over every well, and the neighbours were watching.
And Abram said unto Lot, Let there be no strife, I pray thee, between me and thee, and between my herdmen and thy herdmen; for we be brethren.
Abram was the older man. God had promised the land to him. He could have claimed the best of it. He did not.

Is not the whole land before thee? separate thyself, I pray thee, from me: if thou wilt take the left hand, then I will go to the right; or if thou depart to the right hand, then I will go to the left.
He gave his nephew first choice. Peace mattered more to him than the best pasture.

And Lot lifted up his eyes, and beheld all the plain of Jordan, that it was well watered every where, before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah, even as the garden of the Lord, like the land of Egypt, as thou comest unto Zoar.
Green fields, running water, easy wealth. Lot chose with his eyes, and it looked like paradise.
Abram dwelled in the land of Canaan, and Lot dwelled in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom. But the men of Sodom were wicked and sinners before the Lord exceedingly.
Lot did not move into Sodom at once. He only pitched his tent toward it. That is how the slow road begins. One tent door, one direction, one small choice at a time.
And Abram was left on the dry hills with the smaller share. Then God spoke to him again. He had given up the green valley, and he had given it up for peace.
Look in every direction, God said. All that you see I will give to you and to your children for ever.
Then Abram removed his tent, and came and dwelt in the plain of Mamre, which is in Hebron, and built there an altar unto the Lord.
Lot chose by what he could see, and slowly walked toward ruin. Abram let go of the best, and received everything God had promised.
Would you give up the better share to keep the peace? Tell me below.
The full story of Abram is coming in the long video. Follow so you do not miss part fifteen.
